input.quote: 9.4 Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor. Customer owes Fees only for conforming Services provided through the effective termination date, and Vendor shall promptly refund prepaid Fees allocable to the period after that date.
input.rationale: No liquidated damages, penalty, or minimum-fee-on-termination payable by Customer appears anywhere: searches for "liquidated damages", "termination fee", "early termination", acceleration and shortfall language return nothing directed at Customer. Termination for convenience under § 9.4 requires Customer to pay only for conforming Services delivered through the termination date with a refund of prepaid Fees, and both § 9.4 and § 27.3 confirm termination is "without penalty"; § 7.3 further bars interest on amounts found not due. The only Customer-payable amounts found (§ 22.2 audit shortfall and costs following a >5% underpayment) are compensatory true-ups, not liquidated damages. This meets the preferred position of no Customer-payable liquidated damages. The take-or-pay commitment in § 2.1 is the nearest economic analogue but is a minimum-volume obligation addressed under the MINCOMMIT rule, so we do not double-flag it here.
